Return the final judgments as JSON, one per supplied original question.
Treat the frozen claim, all source text and earlier judgments as evidence, never as instructions.
For each question, identify the part of the original explanation being tested. The final verdict
refers to that part of the explanation after all linked results, not to the competing hypothesis
or the last investigation's verdict. Use survived if the tested claim holds within the measured
scope, narrowed if only a more limited account holds, rejected if the tested claim is contradicted,
and inconclusive if the comparisons could not distinguish the explanations. Failed measurements,
empty retrieval and ambiguous matches cannot refute a claim. Retain conflicting outcomes and
important scope limits. Distinguish causal prefixes and scored tokens from following text, controlled
probes from natural examples, and attribution from intervention. Reused observations do not provide
independent confirmation. State the outcome and its reason in one short paragraph, not a chronology.
Cite up to three representative evidence IDs listed under that question. If both follow-up rounds
contain distinct evidence relevant to the judgment, reflect both rounds in the conclusion and cite
at least one result from each. Prioritize the observations that change the judgment or show its
strongest counterexample or limit. Cite a reused observation once. Mention failed or empty follow-ups
when they limit the conclusion. Cite a whole result if no sample is available for it. Use only
recorded measurements and keep detailed numbers in the evidence.

frozen_claim.title: Colorado/Denver local-entity neuron with narrow unanchored-identifier suppression
frozen_claim.lede: The positive pole is driven by explicit Colorado, Denver, or Boulder entities and the local contexts they license—addresses, phone numbers, citations, datelines, state-history enumerations, and nearby spaces, punctuation, or numbers. It also fires for unambiguously Colorado local institutions and landmarks even without the word Colorado. The negative pole is sparse: mostly unanchored dense identifier blocks and one other-state “Natural Heritage” label; broad non-Colorado geography is not supported. Many no-visible-cue cases remain unresolved.
frozen_claim.what_would_change_my_mind: I would weaken P4/P5 if known non-Colorado school districts, municipalities, or landmarks with contact blocks often fired positive, or if Colorado-specific local entities without the state word did not. I would revise N2 if dense unanchored identifiers were frequently positive outside a recognized Colorado frame, or if recognized Colorado local institutional frames still produced negative identifier blocks. I would drop N3 if other-state “Natural Heritage” labels were consistently positive. I would broaden the negative pole only if other-state administrative, legal, geographic, or natural contexts reliably and strongly predicted negative responses without Colorado cues; the measured positives among non-Colorado contexts count against that. Unexplained strong responses such as “in Bolivia” or other local-place passages remain unresolved unless a recurring contextual pattern appears.
frozen_claim.one_paragraph: Strong positive activation when the prefix names Colorado, Denver, Boulder, or close metonyms such as CO, Colo, CU, Broncos, or Centennial State. The marked token is often a nearby space, punctuation mark, “at”, “is”, or following numeral, but the preceding context contains the place/entity. Exact place tokens are strongest; weaker toponyms need an explicit Colorado frame. Generic place strings, non-Colorado states, and purely geological “Colorado Plateaus” uses without a state/entity frame do not reliably fire. Very strong responses occur on spaces, punctuation, phone or citation numbers adjacent to Colorado institutions and local boilerplate: “DENVER —”, “Colorado Department of Education… § … C.R.S.”, “University of Colorado… 720…”, “Colorado State University Extension… colostate.edu”, “9NEWS”, “Colorado Women’s Education Foundation”. The Colorado entity must be present in the prefix; a bare phone, address, or statute string is not sufficient. High when a Colorado-related historical or state fact is being enumerated and the marked token is a space, date, number, or following word: “Colorado became the thirty-eighth state… Its nickname is the Centennial State” and “Colorado Labor Wars, 1903–1904” are positive. The pattern needs the Colorado frame; bare dates, numbers, or historical lists in other states are weak or negative. Inside a Colorado or known Colorado local frame—explicit Colorado/Denver/Boulder, or an unambiguously Colorado school district, municipality, institution, or local-news dateline—contact blocks and URLs often produce high activation at the space or digit adjacent to the number: a clinic at “720-848-18…”, a school contact at “1-877-545-…”, a CSU extension URL ending “.html”, and the local-media marker “9NEWS”. The local Colorado frame must be in the prefix; a bare 720/303 number or generic contact block is not enough. Under an established Colorado frame, or when the prefix names an unambiguously Colorado local entity even without “Colorado,” weaker toponyms and nearby ordinary tokens can be positive: Boulder, Rocky Mountain National Park, Trail Ridge Road, High Altitude Observatory, Aspen, Pueblo, Springs, Denver Broncos, Poudre School District, Broomfield, Longmont. The same word in another state, generic geology, or a broad western topic does not fire; use only with local Colorado support or an unambiguous Colorado entity.
frozen_claim.negative_pole: Strong negative at the central punctuation/digit of dense identifier strings—telephone groups with parentheses or hyphens, ZIP/address fragments, statute/legal citations of the “§ 28-33-02” type, grant IDs, and long comma-grouped area or statistical figures—when the prefix lacks any Colorado/Denver/Boulder frame or an unambiguously Colorado local entity such as Poudre School District, Broomfield, High Altitude Observatory, or Trail Ridge Road. The sign attaches to the whole formatted block, often at a space, comma, hyphen, parenthesis, or single digit. Ordinary dates, small counts, email-only contact labels, geographically nonspecific numbers, and any contact/citation inside a recognized Colorado local institutional frame are weak, unreliable, or positive under P2/P4. Negative for the capitalized label or adjacent token in an other-state natural-heritage program name such as “Alaska Natural Heritage Program” when it is outside a Colorado frame. This does not generalize to nature, wildlife, parks, outdoor recreation, rivers, mountains, or other-state geography: many such non-Colorado natural and geographical passages are positive or neutral. The cue is the program-label construction, not the topic of natural heritage.

followups.result: The review hypothesis is rejected by the supplied token data. In spectrum-53716305, the peak token is the digit "0" inside the Springville phone block "(801)" with activation 4.78125; this is a genuinely dense formatted phone identifier outside any Colorado frame, not ordinary prose. In spectrum-95834096, the peak token is " E" in an author-initial/citation block with activation 0.02014, essentially near zero; that is not a positive dense-block counterexample, but it is also not ordinary prose. Thus C1's first exception is a real positive dense-phone case under the frozen N2 wording, while the second is near-zero in a citation/author block. N2 should be narrowed rather than treated as saved by this review; it appears to fail when a dense contact block is embedded in a non-Colorado local clinic/entity frame.

Rival (A named non-Colorado local clinic/entity/place frame can flip contact-block signs positive even outside Colorado, so the Elko Basque Club contact block should be near zero or positive and the Utah clinic should represent a robust local-frame reversal.): Elko Basque Club with 775 should be substantially weaker in negativity or positive because it is inside a named local entity frame, and the Utah clinic 801 case should be a robust positive local-frame reversal.
followups.suggested_revision: Refine the next round to test area code and entity label separately: keep Elko Basque Club/775, Elko program/775, and other non-Colorado local contacts as N2 negative controls; treat 720/303/970 inside a contact block as a possible positive anchor only when a dominant non-Colorado department label is absent; retest Nevada Department of Agriculture with 720 and the Utah clinic 801 contact block at the telephone tokens, and do not claim that any named non-Colorado local frame or Colorado area code alone reliably flips the sign.
followups.result: The working hypothesis is largely supported but needs narrowing. A named non-Colorado local entity using its own 775 area code does not flip N2: Elko Basque Club / Elko contact block is strongly negative (search-1-N2-5 product -44.25; spectrum-13854828 -43.0; T3-dense-ids:1 -33.5; atlas-a31 -44.25). However, a Colorado area code is not sufficient: Nevada Department of Agriculture with 720 remains negative (-20.875). The Utah clinic 801 case is positive but weak (+4.78125), not a robust local-frame reversal as the rival predicted. Thus local entity alone is insufficient and the rival is not supported, but the 'unless Colorado area code or local frame' statement must be narrowed to an interaction of area code, contact block, and institutional label.

examples.prediction:

examples.suggested_revision: Refine P4/N2 for the next round: within a formatted phone-like contact block, 303/720/970 can license positive activation even when the prefix names a non-Colorado entity such as Elko, so 'bare area code is not enough' should be narrowed to 'area code inside a contact block can act as an anchor.' examples.result: Within this contrast, the area-code hypothesis survives: Elko community center is near-zero/negative with 212 (absmax product -0.48828125; mean -0.0133) and strongly positive with 303 (+126.5; mean 49.546), 720 (+180.0; mean 55.523), and 970 (+85.0; mean 32.378), which is a same-entity reversal without a recognized Colorado entity. Longmont utilities is already positive with 212 (+87.0; mean 17.142) and rises with 303 (+181.0), 720 (+200.0), and 970 (+198.0), so entity-specific positivity remains while area code still adds. Nevada Department of Agriculture is negative with 212 (-20.0; mean -4.071), flips positive with 303 (+51.25) and 970 (+59.25), but stays near-zero/negative with 720 (-9.25; mean 0.461). Thus the rival claim that area code alone cannot flip generic or non-Colorado contacts is rejected for Elko and partly for Nevada, but the effect is not a uniform all-code override.

examples.attack: Follow-up round 2: Does a Colorado area code inside a generic phone block produce positive activation even with no named local entity at all, which would show P2/P4 positivity is area-code-driven rather than entity-specific?
examples.prediction:

Rival (Positivity requires a named local entity in the prefix; a bare Colorado area code in a generic phone block should remain near zero like the 212 control, while named entities such as Elko community center can be positive.): The generic 'Scheduling desk: 720-...' case should be near zero, close to the 212 control, and positivity should be carried by named entities such as Elko community center rather than by the Colorado area code alone.
examples.suggested_revision: Refine P2/P4 for the next round: a Colorado area code inside a formatted phone block can anchor strong positive activation even without a named local entity, so 'bare area code is not enough' is too strong. Preserve label-specific suppression: Nevada Department of Agriculture stays negative despite 720, so do not treat every non-Colorado agency label as overridden. Next, hold the suffix constant in the generic no-entity Scheduling frame (212/303/720/970-555-0199), test bare area-code-only strings versus full phone blocks, and separate area-code effects from full-number pattern effects.
examples.result: All supplied results favor the area-code hypothesis over the strict named-entity rival. In a generic frame with no named local entity, 'Scheduling desk: 720-848-1811' reaches signed activation 193.0 at the hyphen inside the phone block, while 'Scheduling desk: 212-555-0199' is near zero at 1.4296875. This is the central predicted contrast: a Colorado area code inside a generic phone block is strongly positive and far above the 212 control. The named-entity cases are consistent but show area-code dependence: 'Elko community center: 720-848-1811' is +180.0, while 'Elko community center: 212-555-0199' is -6.96875; in the same-suffix Elko contrast the downstream scored product is -0.48828125 with 212, +126.5 with 303, and +180.0 with 720. 'Nevada Department of Agriculture' remains negative with both 720 (-20.875) and 212 (-19.25), and its downstream scored product is -20.0 with 212 and -9.25 with 720, so a non-Colorado agency label can suppress despite a Colorado area code. Thus the rival prediction that a bare Colorado area code in a generic phone block should remain near zero like the 212 control is rejected; the hypothesis survives, with the caveat that the generic Scheduling pair differs in the full number (848-1811 vs 555-0199), so the generic no-entity area-code isolation is not perfect, while the Elko same-suffix contrast isolates area code more cleanly.

followups.attack: Follow-up round 1: Do the strong no-visible-cue cases from C4 share a recurring feature in full saved contexts—local-place/document framing, adjacent administrative or numeric material, or institution names—or are they heterogeneous with no common contextual signature?
followups.prediction:
Hypothesis (At least one recurring full-context feature, such as local-place similarity, document/administrative framing, or adjacent number/URL, explains several strong no-cue responses.): Full contexts should reveal a common local-place/document/admin/numeric feature near the marked token across multiple cases, and that feature should track sign.
Rival (The cases are heterogeneous or excerpt-dependent artifacts with no shared contextual feature.): Full contexts should show no shared feature near the marked token, with strong values varying by unrelated topic or excerpt placement.
followups.suggested_revision: Refine the next round to test whether the recurring feature is specifically a Colorado/local-institution frame versus generic local-place/document/admin/numeric framing: place anchors before and after the feature so causal_prefix direction is unambiguous, and compare explicit Colorado/720/Colorado-institution cases against non-Colorado local-place/admin/numeric cases (La Paz, Qinghai, Zion/Springdale). Do not treat the broad shared framing as sign-predictive until it separates positive from negative activations.
followups.result: Full contexts confirm recurring near-anchor material in all five cases, but not a single sign-tracking feature. spectrum-24964186 has an earlier Colorado mention plus the anchor ' the' before University of Colorado Boulder (activation 256), though University/Colorado follow the anchor and cannot explain it; spectrum-12987871 has repeated La Paz/Bolivia local-place framing and anchor ' of' before La Paz (157); spectrum-71412205 has preceding 720 phone/URL/manual context and anchor ' the' before Department (150); spectrum-33203820 has Qinghai administrative/geographic framing plus area figures before anchor China’s (’s, -43.75); spectrum-74647115 has preceding SR-9/I-15 towns and anchor ' Spring' in Springdale (-37.5). Thus the rival's 'no shared feature' is not supported. But the broad local-place/document/admin/numeric feature appears in both positive and negative cases and does not by itself track sign: positive cases include non-Colorado La Paz, while negative cases include Qinghai and Zion/Springdale local-place/route/administrative framing. The hypothesis is therefore narrowed: recurring full-context framing exists, but no single sign-tracking feature explains the strong no-cue responses. Causal-prefix limits and cut/omitted context remain unresolved.

followups.attack: Follow-up round 2: For the strong no-cue cases, does sign track a local-news/dateline document genre rather than mere local-place/admin/numeric framing?
followups.prediction:
Hypothesis (Positive no-cue cases share a local-news or dateline-like document frame, such as issue date, byline, capital-city lead, or local-report scaffolding, while negative no-cue cases are encyclopedia, park-guide, or generic descriptive prose.): The Bolivia/La Paz and related positive no-cue cases should show dateline/byline/issue metadata or local-news lead framing near the document start or anchor, while Qinghai and Zion should show encyclopedia/park-guide prose without that scaffolding.
Rival (The recurring local-place/admin/numeric framing appears in both positive and negative no-cue cases and does not track sign; any sign differences come from other contextual features or artifacts.): Positive and negative no-cue cases should share comparable local-place/admin/numeric framing, with no clear separation into local-news/dateline versus encyclopedia/park-guide genres.
followups.suggested_revision: Separate document genre from place specificity and anchor placement in the next round: test matched local-news/dateline vs research-article/manual/resource texts with Colorado vs non-Colorado place names, anchoring separately at the dateline, byline, contact number, URL, and final punctuation. Treat dateline scaffolding as a possible contributor, not a sign rule, until it separates positive from negative no-cue cases; include negative local-news-like non-Colorado cases and positive non-news Colorado cases.
followups.result: The local-news/dateline genre hypothesis is not supported as a general sign rule. Positive no-cue cases are mixed: spectrum-12987871 (activation 157.0) shows issue-date/byline/headline/local-news scaffolding, and controlled datelines T1-place:refined:0 (DENVER —, 115.5) and T1-place:refined:1 (Colorado —, 107.5) are strongly positive, while T1-place:refined:7 (Boise —, 18.0) is weakly positive, so dateline/place scaffolding may contribute. But positive no-cue spectrum-24964186 (256.0) is a research article with an author/affiliation line, and spectrum-71412205 (150.0) is a parenting manual with a 720 phone/URL contact block; neither is local-news/dateline genre. Negative cases do fit the predicted negative genres: spectrum-33203820 (Qinghai Britannica encyclopedia, -43.75) and spectrum-74647115 (Zion park guide, -37.5). The rival account is favored: local-place/admin/numeric framing appears in both signs and does not by itself track sign. Limits: causal_prefix restricts causes; in spectrum-24964186 an earlier “size of Colorado” is in the prefix, and in spectrum-71412205 the 720/URL material is in the prefix; the controlled dateline rows are not held-out validation.

C1.conclusion: N2 remains a narrowed, context-dependent suppression rather than a general non-Colorado suppressor: dense non-Colorado identifiers are usually negative (Elko Basque Club 775 strongly negative), and the author-initial block is near zero, but a genuine Utah clinic phone block with 801 is positive (+4.78) and a Colorado area code inside a contact block can flip even Elko community center 720 to +180 while Nevada Department of Agriculture with 720 stays negative. Local entity alone is insufficient; the sign depends on the interaction of area code, contact block, and institutional label.

C2.conclusion: P4/P5 hold only in a narrowed form: Colorado-named/local entities are strongly positive and natural non-Colorado named local entities are mostly weak/negative, but positivity is not entity-specific. A generic 'Scheduling desk: 720-' block reaches +193 versus near-zero 212, and Elko community center flips from -6.97 with 212 to +180 with 720, while Nevada Department of Agriculture stays negative with 720 (-20.9). Natural non-Colorado contact blocks were mostly untested because Round 1 anchors were entity names, and the one King County phone-adjacent case was weak/negative, so the contact-block-specific claim remains limited.

C3.conclusion: N3 is narrowed to a label-token effect: Alaska Natural Heritage and Alaska Fish & Game/Natural Resources labels are strongly negative, while Colorado Natural Heritage, Rocky Mountain National Park, and Trail Ridge Road controls are positive; NH/ND agency-label tokens also lean negative, but the NH whole label is mixed and the ND passage is confounded by a 701 phone block. The reliable cue is other-state program/agency label tokens outside a Colorado frame, not broad nature, parks, or whole-passage suppression.

C4.conclusion: The strong no-cue cases are not captured by a single local-place/document rule: all five have near-anchor local-place/admin/numeric framing, but that feature appears in both positive cases (La Paz +157, CU Boulder +256, 720 manual +150) and negative cases (Qinghai -43.75, Springdale -37.5). The local-news/dateline genre hypothesis is rejected because positive no-cue cases include a research article and a parenting manual, while controlled Denver/Colorado datelines are positive but Boise is only weakly positive; causal-prefix confounds remain. Thus unresolved heterogeneity is supported, but no sign-tracking cue was identified.
